title: Keep each person, their sessions and the whose-it-is of every record, for training, without anything that identifies or lets in
request: In the storing phase, store each user and their sessions tied to the account, and their actions, decisions and logs: everything capturable, for training and fine-tuning.
spec: With accounts on, events carry ids.user, but the store kept no account table (those tables were never exported) and its records said nothing about whose they were beyond events.
plan: A people keeper over the account tables by named columns, kind sessions, prefix people/
The shapers lift the user onto every record and provenance.by
service/people.json: one row per person per workspace, aggregates beside
Plants for the secrets the tables hold, run against PostgreSQL

decisions.decision: The email is kept only as a salted hash, and the salt lives beside the store (store.people/state.json), never in it.
decisions.why: The store is pushed to GitHub: an unsalted hash of an email can be matched against a list of emails.

decisions.decision: A person who leaves stays in the log as a removed event; nothing is rewritten.
decisions.why: The owner's rule: the store keeps what was kept; only the audited forget removes.

decisions.decision: An existing kind (sessions, prefix people/) rather than a new one.
decisions.why: A new kind needs the core contract, the schemas and every set's filters changed; the type (person, session) separates them.

decisions.decision: A workspace without improve or train consent keeps counts only.
decisions.why: As the database keeper: consent governs, a friend's own workspace is governed by their own.

change: store/keepers/people.py (new), keepers/standard.py, keepers/database.py (docstring), shapers.py (LIFT, RENAME, _type, provenance.by, shapers-4), service.py (people, write), catalog.py, tests/test_store_people.py, the plan.

findings.defect: The account tables hold six kinds of secret and personal value that must never reach the pushed store.
findings.scenario: A keeper that exported app_user, user_session and api_token rows would push password hashes, session digests, token hashes, emails, names and SSO subjects.
findings.cause: The tables were excluded by not being listed, with nothing else enforcing it.
findings.fix: A keeper that selects named columns only (existence of a password or subject as a boolean), hashes the email and the session id with a salt kept off the store, and drops names and token names.

measurements.name: Plants against PostgreSQL
measurements.gate: none of 12 planted values is in raw or records
measurements.result: the password, cookie, request token, digest, API token, token hash, password hash, email, name, subject, a token's name and an SSO user's name: none present; people and sessions present by pseudonymous id
limits: make store-check has no database, so the plants run in the PostgreSQL test only

outcome: Each person and session is kept by pseudonymous id and joined to their records; no secret reaches the store.
lessons: A table kept out by omission is not kept out: name the columns that go in.
risks: A per-person aggregate of where they stalled needs the engagements to carry the user.
